draft.title: Annuities
card: An annuity is an investment that pays out a regular amount each period. The balance earns interest, but the payouts take money out, so the balance falls until it reaches zero.
Each period: new balance = old balance + interest − payout. Interest is worked out on the old balance.
Example: $10 000 earns 6% per year and pays out $2000 at the end of each year. Interest = 6% × 10 000 = $600. New balance = 10 000 + 600 − 2000 = $8600.
If the payout is bigger than the interest, the balance falls. If the payout is smaller than the interest, the balance would rise, so it would not be run down to zero.
draft.remember: Annuity: balance + interest − payout each period, so the balance falls.

a.q: An annuity of $20 000 earns 5% per year and pays out $3000 at the end of each year. What is the balance after the first payout?
a.why: Interest = 5% × 20 000 = $1000. New balance = 20 000 + 1000 − 3000 = $18 000. Taking away only the payout gives $17 000, which leaves out the interest.
a.clue: Add the interest first, then take off the payout.

b.q: Priya's annuity of $50 000 earns 4% per year. It pays out $6000 at the end of each year. What is the balance after two payouts?
b.why: Year 1: interest is $2000, so the balance is 50 000 + 2000 − 6000 = $46 000. Year 2: interest is 4% × 46 000 = $1840, so the balance is 46 000 + 1840 − 6000 = $41 840. This is not among the options, so check: 46 000 + 1840 − 6000 = 41 840, which means the listed answer is wrong.
b.clue: Work out the interest again on the new balance in year 2.

final.title: Annuities
card: An annuity is an investment that pays out a regular amount each period. The balance earns interest, but the payouts take money out, so the balance falls until it reaches zero.
Each period: new balance \(=\) old balance \(+\) interest \(-\) payout. Interest is worked out on the old balance. Repeat for the next period, starting from the new balance.
Example: $10,000 earns 6% per year and pays out $2000 at the end of each year. Interest \(= 6\% \times \$10{,}000 = \$600\). New balance \(= \$10{,}000 + \$600 - \$2000\), which is $8600.
If the payout is bigger than the interest, the balance falls. If the payout is smaller than the interest, the balance would rise, so it would not be run down to zero.
final.remember: Annuity: balance \(+\) interest \(-\) payout each period, so the balance falls.
